name: Dana Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Cliff-dwelling ibex, wolves and juniper where mountains drop to desert.

tip.title: Fail the winter rains
tip.text: The reserve drops from a high plateau to the low desert. Set Winter rainfall to -100% and watch the grasses and trees, then the ibex, birds and predators that rely on them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Wild barley
nodes.desc: A wild grass that GBIF records often in the reserve. Seed-eating birds such as blackbirds are recorded eating barley in GloBI.

nodes.name: Phoenician juniper
nodes.desc: An evergreen tree of the reserve highlands. Its berry-like cones are mainly spread by birds that eat them.

nodes.name: Mount Atlas mastic tree
nodes.desc: A tough tree of dry hill country that is recorded in the reserve. GloBI records blackbirds eating from it.

nodes.name: Acacia
nodes.desc: Thorny acacia trees grow in the warm lower parts of the reserve. Nubian ibex browse their leaves, rearing up or climbing into the branches.

nodes.name: Nubian ibex
nodes.desc: A cliff-dwelling wild goat that eats grasses and acacia leaves. Captive breeding and reintroduction rebuilt its Jordan population, and Dana is a stronghold.

nodes.name: Rock hyrax
nodes.desc: Lives in colonies in rocky crevices and eats a wide range of plants. In the Middle East few land predators take it, helped by its sentries and refuges.

nodes.name: Tristram's jird
nodes.desc: A burrowing rodent that eats seeds and leaves. One of the most-recorded mammals in the area, and small prey for many predators.

nodes.name: Chukar
nodes.desc: A rocky-slope game bird that eats a broad range of seeds and some insects. Golden eagles sometimes prey on it.

nodes.name: Tristram's starling
nodes.desc: The most-recorded bird here. It eats fruit and insects, nests on cliffs, and likely spreads desert plant seeds over long distances.

nodes.name: Eurasian blackbird
nodes.desc: A thrush that GloBI records eating barley and Pistacia atlantica. It is itself prey for foxes, jackals and kestrels.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A small canid recorded in the area. GloBI lists it eating chukar, Tristram's jird and blackbirds.

nodes.name: Golden jackal
nodes.desc: An opportunistic canid. GloBI lists it eating chukar, jirds and blackbirds, and it also scavenges carrion.

nodes.name: Eurasian kestrel
nodes.desc: A small falcon, recorded here nearly 200 times. GloBI lists jirds and blackbirds among its prey.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: A raptor recorded in the area. GloBI lists chukar and rodents such as the jird among its prey.

nodes.name: Arabian wolf
nodes.desc: The area's top predator. It takes ibex and smaller prey such as rodents and birds, and eats carrion. Wolves in Jordan are persecuted for killing livestock.

nodes.name: Caracal
nodes.desc: A cat Wikipedia lists as a threatened native of Dana. Small mammals make up most of its diet, and it can leap to catch birds.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong sun and dry heat drive plant growth in the lower, desert parts of the reserve.

nodes.name: Winter rainfall
nodes.desc: Rain on the high plateau feeds the grasses and trees of the slopes. Dana drops from about 1,500 m to the low desert of Wadi Araba.

nodes.name: Rocky soil
nodes.desc: Thin soils on rock and sandstone slopes hold the reserve's 703 recorded plant species.

nodes.name: Soil microbes & insects
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
